campaigns.title: The persisted edge kind is the edge's kind, and a missing one is refused

mutants.breaks: the store reads the key the engine does not write, so every edge is stored as CALLS -- measured before the fix as 108 CONTAINS edges all typed CALLS, a call graph the repository never had

mutants.breaks: a missing or undeclared kind is written to the column instead of refused, so a None or a typo becomes an edge type no reader can interpret and no gate can see

the engine names the attribute itself instead of importing the shared constant, which is exactly how the original defect arose -- two modules independently choosing what to call the same thing, each self-consistent and neither able to see the other

campaigns.title: An edge the rebuilt graph no longer holds does not survive

mutants.breaks: the clear loop never runs, so INSERT OR REPLACE leaves every departed edge in place forever -- a retired call stays a dependency and the set only grows

mutants.breaks: every service's edges are deleted by any build, because graph_edges carries no service_name and the node ids are the only thing scoping the sweep

campaigns.title: A relative import names a module, and a relative import is internal

mutants.breaks: every relative import reports the imported SYMBOL instead of the module, so a real dependency resolves to no file and reads as an unknown one -- 27 such imports in this repo's own src
a relative import's root is the empty string, which is absent from the stdlib list and is not specweaver, so any package using relative imports infers the adapter archetype instead of pure-logic
the mapper receives no imports, so IMPORTS edges cannot be built at all -- the state the graph shipped in, where nine kinds were declared and one was written

the file-level `imports` key is missing on every early return -- an unreadable file, a symlink, a language with no parser -- so a consumer must guess whether absent means no imports or a writer that predates the field

campaigns.title: An import becomes an edge to the file it names, or to a ghost

mutants.breaks: no IMPORTS edge is built at all, which is the state the graph shipped in: nine kinds declared, one written
an import outside the parsed set produces nothing instead of a ghost, so a traversal cannot tell 'nothing imports this' from 'its importer is outside what we parsed'
two collected files matching one import resolve to whichever sorts first, so a name collision becomes a dependency that looks exactly like a real one -- ADR-006 makes the graph the truth store
a package is only ever matched as a module file, so every import of a directory with an __init__ becomes a ghost
a leading segment that is not a directory -- rust's `crate`, a source root -- stops the module resolving, so whole languages ghost silently

campaigns.title: A file the build could not read is visible on its node

mutants.breaks: a file nobody could open looks exactly like a file with nothing in it, so a traversal returning no edges has two meanings and the reader cannot tell which
a grammar that raised leaves no record, so a whole file's dependencies are silently absent from the graph
the seam knows the file failed and the graph does not, so the fact dies at the boundary it was discovered on
the marker is present on every node, so it distinguishes nothing -- a flag that is always set carries no information at all

campaigns.title: A parser separates extension from implementation, and refuses to guess where it cannot

mutants.breaks: Java's super_interfaces are dropped, so a language whose grammar states the distinction plainly loses it anyway -- exactly the flattening extract_framework_markers already does and that FR-4 exists to avoid

Kotlin supertypes are split by position, which is right for ordinary code and silently wrong for `by` delegation or a base with no explicit constructor call -- a wrong IMPLEMENTS edge looks exactly like a correct one
`Base<T>` reports a dependency on the type parameter T as well as on Base, so every generic supertype invents an edge to a type that does not exist

the next language to declare TYPE_DECLARATION_NODES without a hook gets a payload missing `implements`, so every consumer that reads both keys breaks on it -- a branch nothing reached until a test was written for it

a decorator argument or a constant built by a call never reaches the graph, so a whole class of real file-level dependencies is silently absent

campaigns.title: The grammars that ship no call query get one held here

mutants.breaks: `obj.deep()` reports a call to `obj` instead of `deep`, so every method call invents a dependency on the receiver and loses the real one
C and C++ hold a function's name inside its declarator, so every call in those languages is attributed to the file rather than to the function that made it
a C++ method's name is a field_identifier, so its calls are attributed to the enclosing class instead of the method -- K rather than K.go, which is a node that exists but is the wrong one

the receiver of a method call is reported as a call too, because a receiver is an identifier -- `obj.deep()` invents a dependency on `obj`. This is the naive pattern, and the reason the constrained one exists

only method calls are seen, so every direct call in Kotlin -- the majority of them -- vanishes from the graph while method calls keep working, which reads as partial coverage rather than a broken query
a method's calls are attributed to `go` rather than `K.go`, so every CALLS edge out of a Kotlin method points from a node hash that does not exist

one language silently stops contributing CALLS edges while every other keeps working, so the graph looks populated and is blind to a whole language -- the composition defect no single language's tests can see

campaigns.title: A graph read back out of the database can be written to it again

mutants.breaks: the loader restores the kind under the column's name while the store reads EDGE_KIND_ATTR, so every edge load_from_db returns is one persist_semantic_digraph refuses -- a graph read out of the database can never be written back, which is the state TECH-070's incremental rebuild produces on purpose
a reloaded edge carries no kind at all, so a traversal cannot tell a call from a containment and the next persist refuses the whole graph

campaigns.title: A real build through the shipped command writes typed edges to disk

mutants.breaks: the parser still finds every call and the seam drops them all, so the persisted graph holds containment and imports only -- the silent-empty result this ticket exists to remove, and invisible to every test that stops at the engine
every import resolves to a ghost instead of the collected file it names, so the edge COUNT is unchanged and the dependency graph points at nothing -- a shape no assertion on totals can see
a call deleted from a real source file keeps its edge on disk forever, so the phantom dependency set only grows across rebuilds

campaigns.title: The builder's module-level crossings are the ones its context.yaml declares

mutants.breaks: the import stays and the declaration goes, which is exactly the state AD-3 was approved to fix and sat in undetected for the whole ticket -- tach cannot see it because tach.toml already permits the crossing and the rule lives only in context.yaml

campaigns.title: An edge to a GHOST says what it could not resolve

mutants.breaks: an unresolved target becomes a hash and nothing else, so a reader sees THAT something is unresolved and never WHAT -- os.getcwd and mystery_call are two indistinguishable ghosts, which is the state this requirement exists to remove
the mapper records the name and the engine drops it before the store ever sees it -- four links each passing their own tests while the chain delivers an empty column
an identifier past the 2KB cap reaches the model validator, which raises inside the mapper where nothing catches it, so one pathological file aborts an entire build -- NFR-6 forbids exactly that

campaigns.title: Go and Rust answer the supertype contract like every other language

mutants.breaks: Go reports no types at all, which is the state this closed -- and the state the old contract test passed over, because a loop across an empty result runs its body zero times and reads as coverage
the missing field name is the whole difference between an embed and an ordinary field, so a struct with five int fields would claim to extend int five times

the shared name-finder takes the FIRST identifier and in `impl Runner for Impl` that is the trait, so the graph asserts Runner implements Runner -- wrong, and self-consistent enough to survive a careless read

Rust spreads one type over `struct Impl;` and every `impl Trait for Impl` block, so assigning lets whichever node the walk reached last erase the others -- and the walk order is an implementation detail nobody controls
